claims.text: A near-equiatomic tungsten–vanadium–chromium refractory HEA can serve as an effective low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
The proposed W–V–Cr composition minimizes the production or persistence of long-lived radioactive isotopes.
The proposed alloy retains excellent high-temperature strength.
The proposed alloy retains excellent irradiation resistance.
The starting material is a refractory HEA in an as-cast or homogenized condition with near-equiatomic proportions of tungsten, vanadium, and chromium.
Vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization is a suitable processing route for the proposed HEA.
Temperatures above 1000°C and fusion-relevant neutron irradiation are representative test conditions for the intended plasma-facing application.
The processed alloy will possess a stable nanostructured multiphase microstructure.
This microstructure will resist radiation-induced defects.
This microstructure will resist irradiation-induced phase degradation.
The selected elements yield only short-lived activation products.
The selected elements form phases that remain stable at high temperature.
Sluggish diffusion is inherent to this HEA and will mitigate structural degradation.
The proposed alloy will have high-temperature mechanical performance comparable to conventional refractory materials.
The proposed alloy will have irradiation resistance comparable to conventional refractory materials.
The proposed alloy will exhibit lower residual radioactivity than conventional refractory materials or standard tungsten alloys.
Standard tungsten alloys typically produce more long-lived induced radioactivity while offering comparable high-temperature performance.
Sufficiently high irradiation dose or temperature may cause phase transformations or segregation that degrade the proposed alloy's performance.
The balance between mechanical stability and low activation depends sensitively on composition and processing conditions.
Tungsten, vanadium, and chromium have established refractory and low-activation characteristics.
